ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, and material shareholder against Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act, OFAC SDN list (due to cross-border USD rails), UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HMT sanctions, and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, in accordance with PCMLTFA section 11.1, FINTRAC guidelines, and Alberta Registry enhanced due diligence norms. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced verification and senior-level approval, with continuous monitoring and re-screening at least quarterly or upon any material change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (online service via authorized service providers; NUANS name search request portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in the English/French alphabets (Latin script) using standard alphanumeric characters; no special symbols other than ampersand, asterisk, percent, comma, hyphen, period, and numbers; transliteration of non-Latin names into English is mandatory. The name must include a legal element: 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'Unlimited Liability Company', or 'ULC'/'U.L.C.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative review with the Director of Corporate Registries within 30 days of rejection via the Alberta Corporate Registry using the 'Name Reservation Review' form, paying the applicable review fee (currently CAD 150), and submitting a written statement explaining why the name should be approved, together with supporting trademarks, business history, or public recognition evidence. If the Director dismisses the appeal, a new name reservation may be submitted with a new NUANS search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the registered office; Alberta Business Corporations Act requires a physical street address in Alberta where statutory and legal process may be served during normal business hours. Virtual mailbox services without a physical location and on-site agent are not accepted. A virtual office arrangement may be available for a physical co-working space that has a real street address and a responsible agent accepting service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual probability for an active Alberta ULC with non-resident management; elevated to 25% when the company operates in a FINTRAC high-risk sector such as affiliate advertising arbitrage, due to enhanced municipal and tax authority on-site verification mandates.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, s. 15 (unlimited liability corporation), ss. 10-12 (incorporation), s. 101 (registered office), s. 104 (directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registry Act, RSA 2000 c R-10)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form AL-INC-01) filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for such consideration as directors determine; no escrow account requirement for incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers named in the Articles of Incorporation be and they are hereby confirmed as the founding shareholders of the Unlimited Liability Corporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board hereby approves the subscription for common shares by the founding shareholders in accordance with the share issuance schedule reflected in the Articles, and that share certificates be issued upon payment of the aggregate subscription price. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the corporation in Alberta be and is hereby established at the address set out in the Articles, and that the board consents to such office being the registered office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors appoint the President, Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer as named in the minutes, with such officers to hold office until the next annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) through a licensed NUANS search house
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name search through a registered NUANS search provider. The corporate name must include 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', or 'U.L.C.' as required under the ABCA. Reserve the approved name for up to 90 days if necessary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing or prohibited, file a new NUANS search with an amended name or request directive from Service Alberta Name Review; pay resubmission search fee if charged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) and appointed legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation in accordance with the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), including the statement that the corporation is an unlimited liability corporation, share classes, restrictions, registered office address, and first directors. Ensure each incorporator executes the Articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Articles are rejected for incompleteness, rectify the defect and resubmit to the Corporate Registry; if amendments are required, obtain director consent and file the amended document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Articles and pay the statutory filing fee through the Alberta Corporate Registry portal. Upon successful processing, receive the Certificate of Incorporation and the corporation number. The corporation comes into existence on the date of the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried for validation errors, contact Corporate Registry support to identify the error; correct and resubmit within the prescribed period. If no certificate issues, expedite via Service Alberta courier service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Corporate Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the corporation / corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 days after the certificate is issued, hold an organizational meeting or adopt written board consents. Pass the first board resolution, adopt corporate by-laws, approve share issuance, select the corporate bank, and establish the registered office records and minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If corporate records are incomplete, remedy by executing supplementary resolutions and ensuring the minute book is complete; late record-keeping penalties may apply under the ABCA, so cure promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the CRA to obtain a Business Number, corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and payroll account if employees are hired. For non-resident shareholders, confirm tax reporting obligations. The registration must be completed within 30 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Corporate legal name and registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the registration due to data mismatch, call the CRA Business Window to reconcile corporate details, correct the registration, or request reopening of a suspended account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing authority of the city/town where the registered office is located (e.g., Calgary Licensing and Community Standards)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify municipal zoning and business licensing by-laws. Apply for a business licence if the ULC maintains a physical office; for fully virtual or home-based operations, confirm whether a home-based business exemption is available. Obtain occupancy and fire safety clearance for the premises.
required_dossiers: Proof of leased or owned premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete, revise the application to describe the online affiliate media buying activity clearly; if refused, request an appeal or variance from the municipal licensing and planning department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – non-industrial digital advertising and media arbitrage service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating licence required under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); a municipal business licence may apply only if physical premises are maintained

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based media buying and affiliate lead generation activities are not listed under Schedule 1 or 2 of the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000 c E-3
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC emissions; comply with municipal wastewater and waste diversion bylaws, and manage electronic waste disposal in accordance with Alberta Recycling Management Authority guidelines

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Workplace health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Alberta); fire safety inspection per Alberta Fire Code and Alberta Building Code; municipal occupancy permit required before use of commercial premises

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); official portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses.html) and Business Registration Online (BRO); provincial corporate income tax for Alberta is administered separately by Alberta Finance and Revenue Services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After the Alberta Corporate Registry issues the ULC incorporation certificate, the ULC must apply for a federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Form RC1 or BRO, selecting the GST/HST account if registration is required. For an Alberta-resident ULC, the CRA BN is the national tax identifier and is generally issued immediately online. Required particulars include the Alberta incorporation number, registered office address in Alberta, fiscal year end, principal business activity code, and ownership/director details. A separate Alberta corporate income tax registration may be required once a permanent establishment in Alberta exists; the same BN is referenced for provincial account setup. Foreign parent entities do not obtain a separate TIN from the ULC; the ULC itself is a domestic taxable entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (eligible for U.S. federal tax check-the-box pass-through treatment; under the Canadian Income Tax Act, an Alberta ULC is a resident corporation taxed at entity level)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box regime. The ULC may be classified as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes under Treasury Regulation Section 301.7701-3 by filing IRS Form 8832, but this election does not alter Canadian tax classification. Relevant Canadian elections include voluntary GST/HST registration under the Excise Tax Act, the closely related corporation election under section 156, and, where appropriate, the Income Tax Act section 216 election for non-resident service providers. Hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.2 and 18.3 apply by statute rather than by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST – Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax; Alberta imposes only the federal GST at 5%, with no provincial retail sales tax or provincial component
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies, measured over any calendar quarter or four consecutive calendar quarters; exceeding the threshold mandates GST/HST registration, while voluntary registration is available for persons below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance gateway, or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada. The CRA accepts electronic invoices if they contain the prescribed information under Excise Tax Act subsection 221(1) and related regulations. EDI and portal-based invoicing are permitted without CRA pre-clearance; no Alberta-specific e-invoicing clearance requirement applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods exported by the supplier are zero-rated under Excise Tax Act section 23. Services, including affiliate media buying and advertising arbitrage, are zero-rated under section 25(1) when supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and the supply is not in respect of real property in Canada or tangible personal property ordinarily situated in Canada. The supplier must retain evidence that the recipient is non-resident and not registered, and that the benefit of the service is realized outside Canada. Input tax credits are generally available for inputs acquired in the course of making zero-rated supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate, Canada Border Services Agency ACI export report, commercial contract or sales invoice, carrier waybill or proof of delivery, non-resident recipient evidence such as Form W-8BEN-E or a certificate of residence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may retroactively reassess a zero-rated export claim if documentary support is inadequate, within the normal four-year reassessment period, extended to seven years for misrepresentation. Penalties can include denial of zero-rating, reassessment of 5% GST, disallowance of input tax credits, interest, and penalties under Excise Tax Act sections 280 and 281 of up to 25% of the additional amount, or an Income Tax Act gross negligence penalty under subsection 163(2) of up to 50% of the understated tax. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion may also follow under Income Tax Act section 239. There is no statutory federal FX repatriation deadline in Canadian law; the 180-day benchmark represents an audit-control and substance-review convention.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) is the central monetary authority; the Minister of Finance controls the Exchange Fund Account under the Currency Act and the Financial Administration Act. Canada has no dedicated foreign exchange administration agency. OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) prudentially supervises Schedule I banks, and FINTRAC enforces the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), which governs EFT reporting, Large Cash Transaction Reports, and cross-border currency reporting. All regulated clearing participants must be OSFI-licensed banks or FINTRAC-registered MSB/fintech entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility on both current and capital account. Exchange controls were abolished in 1951; no permits, registration requirements, exchange rate approvals, or convertibility quotas apply to inbound equity, shareholder loans, trade settlements, or profit repatriation. The CAD floats freely. Remittance friction is purely fiscal: dividends paid by the Alberta ULC to non-resident shareholders attract Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, generally reduced to 5%-15% under the Canada-US Tax Treaty) and require CRA Form NR4 filings; arm's-length interest is typically 0% withheld under treaty. Cross-border digital advertising services (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810) are export services, fully remittable without ministerial approval. The Investment Canada Act notification regime applies only to acquisition of control of an existing Canadian business and does not affect greenfield share capital injections into a newly incorporated ULC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no surrender, forced conversion, or mandatory repatriation of export/service receipts. The ULC may retain USD and other convertible currency receivables in Canada or in approved foreign correspondent accounts at its discretion. The only obligations are reporting: FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Reports and Cross-Border Currency or Monetary Instruments Reports for physical movements of CAD 10,000 or more; and bank-level electronic funds transfer reporting on all wire transfers as part of ordinary record-keeping under the PCMLTFA. Ad-network receivables from Google, Meta, and affiliate networks are treated as ordinary service export proceeds and are outside any surrender or export-control regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM for domestic FINTRAC-registered MSB fintechs (Wise, Payoneer Canada); LOW for offshore digital EMIs (Mercury, Revolut Business in non-AB jurisdictions, EU EMIaaS platforms). Wise Payments Canada Inc. may open a multi-currency USD/CAD/EUR/GBP business account for an Alberta ULC using fully remote KYC, provided the ULC holds a CRA Business Number, Alberta corporate registry extract, UBO declaration, and director identity pack; Wise is acceptable only as an overlay for own-account outbound micro-payments and FX conversion, not as the primary settlement bank for high-volume advertiser receipts. Mercury does not onboard Canadian legal entities without a US EIN and US operational address, and its US-only utility makes it legally unsuitable for a non-resident ULC treasury. Offshore EMIs generally lack OSFI-regulated correspondent relationships, are treated as high-risk counterparties by Schedule I banks, and may create FINTRAC MSB classification exposure if the ULC channels third-party flows through them. Legal mitigation: position the ULC as principal in all media procurement contracts so that payment flows are on its own account; this avoids triggering the Canadian MSB licensing regime under the PCMLTFA.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory physical-presence mandate exists for a provincially incorporated Alberta ULC. The PCMLTFA Client Identification Procedures (sections 63-69) and FINTRAC guidance permit electronic identity verification, including credit-bureau verification, notarized passport copies, and bank video-KYC, so directors may onboard remotely from outside Canada. In practice, Schedule I banks will accept remote opening for a domestic private corporation, but a non-resident (e.g., United States) controlling director usually triggers Enhanced Due Diligence requiring a single authorized-compliance video interview or, in some cases, an in-person activation meeting at an Alberta branch for first-time authorizers. The ULC should designate at least one Authorized Representative with a Canadian residential or registered-office address for service of process and delivery of banking devices. Budget 3-8 weeks for onboarding in EDD cases, and execute the Account Opening and Borrowing Resolution with a FINTRAC-compliant e-signature platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident (United States) beneficial ownership combined with the unlimited liability charter and potential US check-the-box pass-through election creates ambiguity about the true economic owners and the entity's liability shield, triggering CDD/EDD review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Alberta Registries Certificate of Status and corporate search; (b) Articles of Incorporation referencing the Alberta Business Corporations Act; (c) UBO declaration naming every 25% or more owner with source-of-wealth statements from US tax filings; (d) if applicable, the US Form 8832 check-the-box election and a Canadian tax lawyer opinion confirming that the ULC remains a 'corporation' for Canadian Income Tax Act purposes; (e) reference letters and account statements from the owners' primary US bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Performance media-buying and affiliate arbitrage model appears as a high-volume commission disbursement hub: inbound wire flows from US/Irish ad platforms followed by dozens or hundreds of outbound payments to overseas publishers, resembling money-laundering layering or an unlicensed money services business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (bundle) (a) signed Insertion Orders and Media Buying Agency Agreements identifying the ULC as principal; (b) ad-network settlement statements (Google Ads, Meta Business Manager, and affiliate networks) covering 12 months of campaign-level revenue; (c) a CPA-prepared funds-flow narrative showing gross-pass-through versus net-margin economics so that round-tripping is not inferred; (d) the beneficiary manifest with legal names, countries, tax identifiers, and invoice references for all recurring payees; (e) a signed AML/Trade narrative letter from the ULC's compliance officer confirming that no virtual assets or cash-courier channels are used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment counterparties in high-risk or sanction-adjacent jurisdictions (e.g., Cyprus, Malta, Latvia, Malaysia, Israel for traffic arbitrage) and the unlimited liability structure double the bank's credit and reputational risk assessment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Ontario/AB corporate registry excerpt confirming the 'ULC' designation and the shareholders' in-solvency-only liability clause; (b) third-party adverse-media and sanctions screening (Refinitiv/World-Check) for the top 20 counterparties; (c) contractual flow-chart proving the ULC does not interface with end consumers; (d) net-worth statements of each UBO to evidence capacity to support the unlimited liability line; (e) a jurisdiction risk matrix prepared by counsel, with policy to terminate counterparties in OFAC/OSFI-listed jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of digital-assets or prepaid-card settlement for affiliate traffic, or attempted use of crypto-friendly foreign EMIs, is a red flag for FINTRAC travel-rule scrutiny and bank transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) a corporate treasury policy memorandum expressly prohibiting virtual-asset settlements; (b) a signed MSB classification self-assessment confirming the ULC only transacts on its own account; (c) bank-side undertaking to route all payouts via SWIFT MT103 or ACSS EFT with a 5-7 day ledger cycle; (d) annual confirmation from a CPA that no cryptocurrency wallets, cash equivalents, or digital-asset exchanges appear in the ULC's books.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections will be effected by SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident parent (or US financing holdco) into the ULC's designated account at an Alberta branch. Recommended ISO 20022/GP purpose codes are 'EQUI' for equity subscription and 'SHLN' for shareholder loan; the payment narrative must read 'Contribution to paid-up capital of [Name] ULC' or 'Shareholder loan - principal' and be backed by a board resolution, share subscription agreement or promissory note, and the CRA T2 schedule for capital. No government permit or exchange-control approval is required. Funds must not originate from third-party pooled accounts, as this would trigger UBO verification and FATCA/CRS red flags. To keep the corporate 'capital escrow' trail clean, segregate the subscription proceeds in a distinct Capital Escrow Account and maintain a separate Operational Account for ad-network inflows. The bank will require CRS/FATCA self-certification and corporate residential-status documentation from the ULC, and US-domiciled payors will require the ULC's Form W-8BEN-E to evidence Canadian tax residence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For Canadian-dollar obligations, use Payments Canada ACSS/ISO 20022 EFT credits or same-day Real-Time Rail (RTR) settlement. For USD and multi-currency trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers through the Schedule I bank's correspondent network (e.g., RBC/BMO USD clearings via their US bank subsidiaries) or commercial cross-border EFT mass-payment files for affiliate commissions. Commercial Letters of Credit are not relevant to performance-media service procurement; the operative instruments are Open Account net-30/60 terms with advertisers plus commercial corporate cards (Visa/Mastercard) for online campaign spend. For low-value international publisher payouts, Wise Business may serve as a tactical overlay, but it should be capped at 25% of monthly aggregate payout volume and reconciled monthly to a single consolidated invoice to keep the audit trail unambiguous. All outbound wires must carry full beneficiary legal name, address, and purpose code 'GDSV' or 'Digital Marketing Services' to satisfy FINTRAC record-keeping and avoid transaction-monitoring holds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable outright forward contracts (1-24 month tenors) executed via a Schedule I bank dealing room
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on select emerging-market currencies (e.g., BRL, MXN, TWD) used for affiliate-payout exposure, with bank-approved counterparties under an ISDA/CSA
Cross-currency swaps (principal-exchange) for intercompany shareholder-loan and funding-maturity hedging
Zero-premium collars and participating forwards to protect USD campaign margins without upfront option premiums
Plain-vanilla FX rollover (Tom-Next) for short-dated working-capital swings, with monthly netting across CAD/USD accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 100; continued non-filing may trigger administrative dissolution by the Registrar and reinstatement costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including Alberta provincial corporate tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the sixth month after the corporation’s fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, prescribed CRA interest, possible director liability for unremitted withholdings, and prosecution for continued non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal corporate declaration confirming registered office, directors, and register accuracy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records; changes are filed with Alberta Corporate Registry as they occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the annual return; director or registered-office changes must be updated within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of statutory registers is an offence under Alberta corporate law; inaccurate declarations may invalidate reliance on corporate records and expose directors to penalty or liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies to distributing corporations, public issuers, and securities-reporting issuers. A private non-distributing Alberta ULC may waive the auditor appointment annually by unanimous shareholder consent; an audit becomes compulsory if the entity distributes securities to the public, becomes a reporting issuer, or lender or regulatory covenants require audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; private enterprises may apply ASPE under CPA Canada Handbook Part II. The financial records must also support T2 compliance and be consistent with the Income Tax Act and Alberta Business Corporations Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ULCs must maintain current members, directors, and beneficial-ownership records where the Alberta beneficial-ownership transparency regime applies. Share transfers affecting significant control must be recorded promptly and confirmed annually through the corporate records and annual return cycle. Failure to update the registers may result in administrative fines and may limit the ability to assert rights against the corporation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200–USD 600 per annum depending on approved Alberta registered agent and registered office provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–USD 8,500 per annum for a private non-distributing Alberta ULC operating an affiliate media-buying scope, where audit is not waived or where lender/regulatory conditions require it

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 11% Alberta general corporate tax rate (federal 15% + provincial 11%, combined headline 26%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 3% small business rate on first $500,000 active business income; no general tax holidays or preferential deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return filed electronically via CRA My Business Account and Alberta provincial return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., June 15 for December 31 year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate revenue from all sources including Canadian operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only Canadian-source income; exclude foreign revenue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue less allowable deductions and losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents limited to Canadian-source income deductions only

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated tax on taxable income at applicable rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply federal and Alberta rates; claim any applicable treaty relief

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty $100 per day up to $25,000; 5% monthly interest on unpaid tax; 50% penalty for gross negligence or underpayment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal withholding tax on dividends to non-residents (Alberta imposes no additional provincial WHT)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TD1 form and supporting documentation to CRA for reduced treaty rate; include Transfer Pricing Ruling or TRC if required
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% federal (treaty rates 0-10%); Interest: 25% federal (treaty rates 0-10%)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory local file; master file required for MNEs with global revenue exceeding CAD 50 million
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP), Resale Price Method, Cost Plus Method, Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM), Profit Split Method
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations do not apply; Canada applies General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance over form principles

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or false statements in tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction with fines up to $1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years; 50% penalty for gross negligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for willful failure to remit taxes; possible imprisonment and director disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length pricing without documentation or economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of income, penalties up to 50% of tax shortfall, interest charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax not remitted; potential criminal charges if fraudulent

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing shell entities to avoid tax or reporting obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR application disallowing deductions; penalties 50% of tax + interest; possible criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal tax liability, fines, and imprisonment for intentional misconduct
